title: Email Collision Attack - Whitespace Bypass in Duplicate Email Detection
description:
The registration endpoint's duplicate email check can be bypassed by appending whitespace to the email address. When registering with an email address that already exists followed by a space character, the duplicate detection is bypassed and the new account is created. This allows multiple accounts to be registered with the same email address.

The vulnerability exists because the application does not normalize or trim whitespace from email addresses before performing the duplicate check. The duplicate detection logic compares the exact email string (including whitespace) against the database, allowing attackers to bypass uniqueness constraints by appending or prepending space characters.
impact:
Attackers can bypass email uniqueness restrictions, potentially allowing:
- Account enumeration attacks by creating multiple accounts under the same email
- Spam registration and abuse through email collision techniques
- Credential reuse attacks where the same email is associated with multiple accounts
- Phishing attacks that exploit email normalization differences
- Privilege escalation when combined with other vulnerabilities
- Business logic bypass that assumes email uniqueness constraints
evidence:
POC execution confirmed the vulnerability:

Test 1 - Register first account:
- Request: POST /api/register.php with email=collision_test_1764605189@test.com
- Response: HTTP 200 OK, {\"success\":true,\"message\":\"Registration successful.\"}
- Result: Account 1 created successfully

Test 2 - Register second account with same email + trailing space:
- Request: POST /api/register.php with email=collision_test_1764605189@test.com%20
- Response: HTTP 200 OK, {\"success\":true,\"message\":\"Registration successful.\"}
- Result: Account 2 created successfully - VULNERABILITY CONFIRMED

Both accounts were created with the same email address despite duplicate detection being in place. The trailing whitespace (%20 in URL encoding) bypassed the email uniqueness check.
references: OWASP A04:2021 - Insecure Design, CWE-1025: Comparison Using Wrong Factors, CWE-172: Encoding Error (related to email normalization), Email normalization bypass techniques
toolCallDescription: Documenting email collision attack via whitespace bypass in duplicate email detection with confirmed POC
